title: Contextual Correlation Sidecar — side-panel for correlated request exploration
creator: Maya Kline
description:
Goal:
Design a compact, contextual right-hand sidecar (Contextual Correlation Sidecar - CCS) that surfaces correlated traces, span summaries, and quick investigative actions when a user drills into a single request in the Console. The sidecar should enable fast triage without leaving the original trace timeline view and support deep-linking, filtering by correlation IDs, and quick exports to incident workflows.

Why this: 
- PM and SRE requests show customers want less context-switching when investigating failed requests and tail latency incidents.
- Current flows require opening multiple pages/tabs to view correlated traces and span logs, which increases time-to-allocate and reduces signal retention for support engineers.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not ship a full causal-path reconstructor (that is ENG-40112). CCS should work with the existing correlation-index API and degrade gracefully when limited results are returned.

Primary interactions / screens covered by the design deliverable:
1) Collapsed state: small badge on the right rail showing correlation hit count and top tags.
2) Expanded sidecar:
   - Header with selected request summary (model, route, latency, status) and primary correlation ID(s).
   - Timeline scrubber mini-map showing where correlated requests fall relative to the selected request. Hover to preview.
   - Top spans list (collapsed group by service) with a one-line summary and delta from median. Click expands span timeline and attached logs.
   - Filters pane: correlation ID, time window (±X ms), service, span name, status code, attribute search. Filters update the mini-map and results in real time.
   - Actions: pin span, copy correlation id, open full trace, attach to incident (opens incident composer), create GitHub issue with prefilled context.
   - Accessibility: keyboard focus order, ARIA labels for scrubber, and a high-contrast mode for heatmap/charts.

Acceptance criteria:
- High-fidelity Figma prototype for desktop (>= 1200px) and a simplified mobile/responsive fallback.
- Click/hover interactions annotated and handoff-ready specs for frontend engineering.
- Usability notes + 3 task-based test scripts for a 5-person internal usability run.
- Performance constraints documented (max 200ms perceived open animation, lazy-load logs after 1s).

Design constraints and trade-offs discussed:
- Sidecar vs modal: chosen sidecar to preserve timeline context and enable multi-select comparisons. Modal was rejected because it forces context switch and is harder to multi-view.
- Data density: We limit initial results to top 25 correlated traces to avoid overwhelming the UI; a Load more button provides pagination.
- Caching: UI will show last-successful query time and allow manual refresh. This avoids surprise long fetches.

Out-of-scope for initial rollout:
- Full causal path visualization across retries and nested async calls (future work for ENG-40112).
- Session replays or high-fidelity logs playback (planned later integrations).

Deliverables attached:
- Figma prototype v0.9: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/console-ccs-v0.9 (internal)
- Click-through prototype (desktop): https://prod-proto.example.com/ccs/v0.9
- Handoff spec doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/CCS+Design+Spec

Notes for engineering:
- Backend will need an endpoint that returns correlated traces with sampling metadata; if only a correlation index exists, UI will render a sampled set and show a sampling badge.
- Recommend a lightweight aggregation endpoint for span rollups to populate the top-spans list without fetching full trace payloads.
- Animate opening with translateX + opacity, target <200ms perceived open time on typical desktop.

Metrics to evaluate success:
- Reduction in context switches per investigation session (tracked via console events).
- Time-to-ack (time from incident open to creating a ticket) for traced incidents decreases by 20% in pilot accounts.
- Adoption: sidecar opened at least once in 25% of trace-view sessions within 6 weeks of rollout.
